Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

advice noun

also good advice, sound advice, on your advice, a bit of advice, piece of advice, take advice, take your advice

classical

Traupman 269, 280

cōnsilium, cōnsiliī n.

noun, second declension

advice, counsel

“Ask someone’s advice” is aliquem cōnsulere; “on your advice”, tē auctōre; “a bit of advice”, aliquid cōnsiliī.

Other words

  • tē auctōre — on your advice, at your suggestion

    ablative absolute · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 1011: tē auctōre quod fēcisset (Lewis & Short s.v. auctor); Traupman 269

Examples

  • rēctum cōnsilium

    good adviceTraupman 269

  • aliquid cōnsiliī

    a bit of adviceTraupman 280

See also suggest, consult, follow.

SourcesLewis & Short: consilium · Lewis & Short: auctor

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 269, 280.
